after.comments_docs:
[Primary] Description quality: precise, voltage-valued, self-describing, and structurally parallel to the accepted sibling electrostatic_potential_at_midplane ('X is the voltage-valued scalar potential of the ... plasma ... relative to a chosen electrical reference'); minor dock for not folding the distinguishing clause into the description itself as midplane does. Documentation quality: opens with 'It is the wall-local restriction of electrostatic_potential', directly mirroring midplane's 'It is the midplane restriction of the plasma ...' — excellent template fidelity; the E_es = -∇Φ equation is correct and standard, the sign convention is stated in prose without referencing COCOS numbers, and the paragraph distinguishing wall-material potential, applied bias, and floating_electrostatic_potential is a strong, correctly-placed exclusion clause; docked only for omitting units on the equation's variables. Completeness: parent link and floating-potential distinction are present and well-integrated, but a cross-reference to the sibling location-variant electrostatic_potential_at_midplane is missing, which same_base/sibling-family context would expect for consistency across the location-restricted potential family. Physics accuracy: all claims verify cleanly — the potential-energy-based sign convention is standard textbook electrostatics, the -∇Φ relation matches the electric_field vector sibling's documented electrostatic contribution, the explicit exclusion of the floating potential (established by zero-net-current) correctly cites that sibling's own definition without contradiction, and there is no implementation leakage (no IDS names, DD paths, or storage references appear in the prose).
[Secondary] Description quality (17): Opening matches the accepted family template used by electrostatic_potential_at_midplane ('Electrostatic potential at {locus} is the voltage-valued scalar potential of the … plasma … relative to a chosen electrical reference'), with only the wall-locus token swapped and quasineutral dropped for genuine near-wall sheath physics. Minor dock versus electron_temperature_at_wall, whose description already packs the material-vs-plasma distinction into the one-liner, and versus electrostatic_potential_at_midplane, whose description also carries the gradient/field clause and an explicit floating/near-wall disambiguation. Documentation quality (16): Section structure parallels the family (definition → wall-local restriction of electrostatic_potential → E_es = −∇Φ → contrasts → sign convention). Equation and sign convention are correct and free of COCOS numbers. Docked because Φ and E_es lack explicit units in the where-clause (siblings that carry gradient equations typically state V and V·m⁻¹) and the nexus language 'wall-local restriction' is slightly less parallel than midplane's 'midplane restriction of the plasma …' phrasing. Completeness (16): Parent link, floating_electrostatic_potential contrast, defining relation, and sign convention are present with no IDS/DD leakage. Docked for omitting a cross-reference to electrostatic_potential_at_midplane (that accepted sibling's description already names near-wall plasma potential as the quantity to distinguish) and for leaving the material-bias contrast in prose only without a sibling-style see-also. Physics accuracy (19): Every definitional claim is consistent with electrostatic_potential, floating_electrostatic_potential, and electrostatic_potential_at_midplane: plasma-side potential (not wall-material bias), E_es = −∇Φ, inductive contribution excluded from this scalar, standard positive = higher potential energy for a positive test charge. Only a negligible under-specification that near-wall 'immediately adjacent' is the plasma side of the sheath rather than a quasineutral evaluation, which is already implicit and physically correct.
